clue.text: Film box office, first to be installed

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word just before it
something installed is fitted inside something else, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a carton is a cardboard box
the opening letter of office

explanation.surface: A film's takings at the box office, with the first one about to go on release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box office' reads as one cinema phrase, but box is the carton and office only lends its initial, which goes into the middle of the carton.
explanation.definitionFit: An animated picture shown in cinemas or on television is a kind of film.

clue.text: Soon to grab free-standing firedog

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing means set upright, so the word reads from bottom to top
to grab means to hold, so the word for soon goes around the other piece

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Soon someone will seize an upright firedog.
explanation.walkthrough: Free-standing reads as one adjective, but it splits: free is the word to reverse, and standing turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is the metal support holding logs in a fireplace, also called an andiron.

clue.text: Characteristic cunning overturned it

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down answer the word for cunning reads upwards

blocks.note: art can mean craft or cunning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Typically, guile has upset the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature, the same as a characteristic.

clue.text: Policemen in charge in advance

definitions.note: plural in the clue, singular answer

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to advance an idea is to offer it
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Senior policemen are in charge ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is a policeman or policewoman, so the plural clue names members of that rank.

clue.text: Refuse to boast about having to grow old

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for boast is read from its end

blocks.note: to brag is to boast
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone declines to brag about getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is rubbish or waste thrown away, the same thing as household trash.

clue.text: New Age Ena reaches an arm of the Mediterranean

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged into a different form

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A New Age traveller called Ena gets to the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the sea between Greece and Turkey, an arm of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Radio cab travelling around one thoroughfare and another

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so these letters change places
around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the first road

blocks.note: the letters of cab
a road is a thoroughfare
St is the abbreviation for street, another thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A radio taxi drives round one road after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio a message is to broadcast it, transmitting over the airwaves.

clue.text: Well-bred fellow, a sometimes shocking swimmer

blocks.note: gent is short for gentleman, a fellow
the electric eel can deliver a shock

explanation.surface: A refined chap who sometimes swims in a shocking manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel describes polite, refined manners typical of good breeding or upper-class upbringing.

clue.text: Innocent disco dancing leads to separation

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so these letters shift around

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Harmless dancing at a disco ends in a couple splitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconnection is the act of cutting a link, a parting or separation.

clue.text: Perfect student dropped off, it's thought!

indicators.note: dropped off means let fall away, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: ideal means perfect
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A model pupil nodded off in class, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropped off suggests falling asleep; here the learner's L simply drops off the end of the word for perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept is something formed in the mind, a thing that has been thought.

clue.text: Rides here just run on shore

blocks.note: fair means just or even-handed
to ground a boat is to run it onto the shore

explanation.surface: Rides at this beach simply run along the seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling funfair site is where people go on roundabouts and other amusement rides.

clue.text: Man admits good books will be somehow stimulating

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the first name holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: a man's first name
OT is the Old Testament, the first part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A man confesses that good books will somehow excite him.
explanation.walkthrough: Good books looks like literature in general, but it is the Old Testament, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexually arousing is stimulating in a particular, sensual way.

clue.text: Dealer caught by animal trainer

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a handler trains and controls animals, such as police dogs

explanation.surface: A trader is captured by a dog handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a trader in supplies, such as a ship's chandler selling equipment for boats.

clue.text: Charming listener coming in close

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a close or conclusion is an ending
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A delightful eavesdropper sidles up near by.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is the noun meaning conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wins affection is charming, lovable and appealing.

clue.text: Are badly stained, but set aside for future use

indicators.note: badly means poorly arranged, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of are
marked means stained or blemished

explanation.surface: Things are badly blotched but have been put by for later.
explanation.walkthrough: Badly stained looks like a single phrase, but badly belongs to are, which it shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked money or goods are designated or reserved for a particular later purpose.

clue.text: Authority takes £2 for an excursion

indicators.note: takes means holds, so the word for authority surrounds the money

blocks.note: to have the say is to have authority
the pound sign is L, from Latin libra, and two of them give a pair

explanation.surface: An official body charges two pounds for a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is an outing or short trip, as in a brief sally into town.

clue.text: Point to firm sailors showing derision

blocks.note: south, a compass point
Co is short for company
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A company's sailors are pointed at and mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and mockery shown towards someone is derision, open disdain.

clue.text: Uproar first caused by Latin love affair

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: the opening letter of caused
L is the abbreviation for Latin
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A scandal first erupted over an Italian romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud outcry or noisy protest, much like an uproar.

clue.text: Drunk I've fed, etc is not working

indicators.note: drunk means staggering about, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A drunkard confesses that after a meal and so on, they are useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty machine is broken and out of order, so it is not functioning.

clue.text: Beg soldiers to go into a tent when changing

indicators.note: to go into means to enter, so the soldiers sit inside the other letters
changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are pleaded with to enter a tent to get changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or implore earnestly, the same as to beg.

clue.text: Type is accepted by no vicar standing

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing means set upright, so the words read from bottom to top
accepted by means taken in, so the little word goes inside

blocks.note: NO plus REV, short for reverend, a vicar
taken as written

explanation.surface: This sort of thing is not welcomed by any vicar in office.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is a particular form or variant of something, a type of it.

clue.text: Half of parish wants a young male priest!

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of its six letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a son is a young male child

explanation.surface: Half the parish is clamouring for a youthful new priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish clergyman, a Church of England priest or vicar.

clue.text: Falls which can blur one's vision

blocks.note: first meaning: a large waterfall
second meaning: a clouding of the eye's lens

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea, spray from a waterfall misting the eyes, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a great waterfall and the eye condition where the lens becomes opaque.

clue.text: The "missing saint" story is just supposition

indicators.note: missing means without, so the abbreviation for saint is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
St is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written

explanation.surface: The tale of a vanished saint is merely conjecture.
explanation.definitionFit: An unproven idea put forward to explain something is a supposition or hypothesis.

clue.text: After getting rid of cold, stopped and relaxed

indicators.note: getting rid of means throwing out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Once the chill was gone, someone stopped and unwound.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, so relaxed in the sense of slackened.

clue.text: People could be seen to somewhere in Kent

indicators.note: could be suggests the words might turn into something else when rearranged

blocks.note: folk means people
the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Locals could be attended to somewhere in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; FOLKESTONE is a port on its coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Folkestone is a Channel port town in Kent, so it is one place in that county.

clue.text: Piano is left in back, an oversight

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the little word is
back means the whole assembled string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A piano got left at the back by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The left L sits inside IS, the piano P goes in front, and the string PILS is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error or lapse, the same thing as an oversight.

clue.text: Cautious pair, you said, tend to go mad

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the pronoun is replaced by the letter that sounds the same
going mad means losing order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: pr is the abbreviation for pair
the letter U is pronounced like you
the letters of tend

explanation.surface: A careful couple are told they're liable to go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wary who acts with care and forethought is prudent, a close synonym.

clue.text: Trainee to dust round hospital department

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of dust
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A trainee cleaner is sent to dust around a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is someone learning a profession, such as a student nurse, so a trainee.
